findings.title: Shared RunObserver keys poll state only by journal entry id
findings.description: `RunnerTenant` creates one `RunObserver` in `__init__` (`src/amoeba/runner/tenant.py:74`) and passes it to every `ProjectTick` (`src/amoeba/runner/tenant.py:133`), but `RunObserver.observe()` starts each call with `live = {entry.id for entry in entries}` and then prunes `_last_poll`, `_overdue`, and `_faulted` to that set. Those dictionaries are keyed only by `entry.id`, not by `(project_id, entry.id)`, and `entries` here is one project's `_run_entries()` (`src/amoeba/runner/tick.py:87-91`). On a normal multi-project tick, observing project B therefore discards project A's poll timestamps, overdue flags, and standing poll faults; the next tick sees A as having never been polled. This defeats the `run_poll_interval_seconds` bound at `src/amoeba/process/settings.py:83` and can close a still-standing escalation via `_close_recovered()` (`src/amoeba/runner/tick.py:195-199`). The multi-project tests in `tests/runner/test_tenant.py` use fresh, untracked entries, so they do not exercise this state carry-over. Key the observer state by project and entry, or give each project its own observer and pass `project_id` into `observe()`.

findings.title: Store failures can be swallowed as unexpected per-project faults
findings.description: `STORE_FAILURES` contains only `StoreBusyError`, `StoreCorruptError`, `StorePermissionError`, `StoreSchemaError`, and `sqlite3.Error`. In `src/amoeba/store/models.py:162-197`, every store error derives from `StoreError`, including `StoreIntegrityError`, `NodeNotFoundError`, and `InvalidTransitionError`; `ValueError` is also used for invalid journal/escalation writes in `src/amoeba/store/journal.py` and `src/amoeba/store/project_escalations.py`. The broad handler at `src/amoeba/runner/tenant.py:142-149` re-raises only `(*STORE_FAILURES, UpstreamShapeError)` and logs/escalates every other `Exception`. A real invariant or transition failure can therefore be converted into a per-project escalation and the process keeps running against a store whose writes are failing. The design states that store failures re-raise so recovery can take over; the guard should cover the store error hierarchy (and any validation error that indicates a bad store write) rather than a partial subclass list.

findings.title: Runner launches/subprocess scheduling has no load-tier coverage
findings.description: The changed code introduces new tick-time subprocess paths: `subprocess.Popen` in `src/amoeba/runner/launch.py`, `poll_run` calls from `src/amoeba/runner/observe.py`, `cf` probes in `src/amoeba/runner/probes.py`, and the start-up `sq` probe in `src/amoeba/runner/factory.py`. The Python rules require at least one load test with latency, throughput, or resource bounds for simulation/network/concurrency/environment-layer paths, gated in CI. `.github/workflows/ci.yml:54` runs `pytest tests/load`, but that tier still exercises only the older host/journaling, recovery-scale, inbox, feed, serve, and CF-watch paths (for example `tests/load/test_crash_loop.py` uses `JOURNALING_TENANT` from `tests/load/load_harness.py`, not `RunnerTenant`). `tests/runner/test_budget_coverage.py` verifies no call starts after a logical deadline, but it is a unit test with a fake clock and does not assert real latency, throughput, subprocess contention, or bounded resource use. Add a load test that drives the Runner with multiple in-flight `sq` polls and/or CF links under a realistic configuration and asserts a latency/throughput/resource bound; gate it in the existing load step.

findings.title: Start-up calls can exceed their configured time bounds
findings.description: `start()` builds the tenant tuple with Python argument evaluation: `standard_tenants(settings, supervisor_dir)` runs first and calls `capture_sq_version_label(settings.sq_timeout_seconds)` and `capture_cf_version_label(settings.cf_timeout_seconds)` (`src/amoeba/process/tenants.py:35-36`), then `runner_tenant()` calls `probe_sq(settings, _now(), poll_run)` (`src/amoeba/runner/factory.py:59`), whose `poll_run` is bounded by `sq_timeout_seconds`. With defaults from `src/amoeba/process/settings.py`, each of these three pre-loop subprocesses can take up to 10 seconds, so startup may spend ~30 seconds before recovery or the loop begins. The `sq --version` label is explicitly an opaque, unavailable-tolerant provenance value (`src/amoeba/process/version_label.py`), and the new `sq` probe already validates that `sq` exists and has the required shape. Removing the redundant `sq --version` capture, or sharing one bounded start-up `sq` check and bounding the total pre-loop phase, would keep the settings' documented timeout behavior honest. The `cf --version` capture could either be shared with the first per-link probe or documented as a separate bound.

findings.title: Stale comments contradict the implemented fault handling
findings.description: The module docstring still says "Escalation writes join this module in a later task," but this diff adds `raise_expected_faults()` at `src/amoeba/runner/faults.py:124-145` and `escalate()` at `src/amoeba/runner/faults.py:152-188`. Likewise, `tests/cli_harness.py:3-6` and `tests/test_cli_lifecycle.py:3-7` claim that `tests/test_cli_safety.py` mechanically proves CLI-test safety; `list_files` shows no `tests/test_cli_safety.py`, while the actual guard is `tests/test_store_safety.py`. These are small but misleading documentation drifts on newly touched files; update them to name the code and guard that actually exist.

structured_findings.summary: Shared RunObserver keys poll state only by journal entry id
Store failures can be swallowed as unexpected per-project faults
Runner launches/subprocess scheduling has no load-tier coverage
Start-up calls can exceed their configured time bounds
Stale comments contradict the implemented fault handling
